schemaNote: Process-level startup smoke plan, consumed by claude-code-app's flagStartupSmoke task. Each case names an entry of gradle/cli-flag-matrix.json and inherits that entry's argv, so a flag can only be smoked under a spelling the parse layer already checks. Optional per-case fields: argv (replaces the entry's argv, the only way to reach a placeholder), prompt (replaces the appended prompt; [] appends none), expectExit (default 0), expectStdout (default the marker when a prompt is appended, otherwise required), expectStderr, expectTranscriptEntries (type/field/value rows that must coexist in the same newly-created JSONL), files (relative path -> content, written under the case's scratch directory), dirs (relative directories created there), note. Placeholders: {{sessionId}} a session already recorded under the isolated HOME, {{scratch}} this case's own directory, {{baseUrl}} the fake Anthropic server.
statusNote: notSmoked exists so every parse-aligned flag carrying an argv is either exercised as a process or has a written reason not to be. ClaudeCodeCliFlagMatrixTest fails when one is neither, which is what keeps this plan from silently falling behind the matrix.

cases.note: The baseline every other case is a variation of: one turn, start to finish, through the packaging under test.

The case this harness was built for. A native image missing reflection metadata for AssistantContent's constructor aborts here and nowhere else, because -c is the only startup path that deserializes a recorded assistant message before the first turn. Only meaningful while the workspace sits outside a git repository: inside one, session lookup resolves through the enclosing repository's worktrees, finds nothing, and starts a fresh session that never touches the recorded message.
The matrix argv names a UUID no session has, which is a parse-level concern; a process needs one that was actually recorded.

cases.expectStderr: Cannot create a worktree: not in a git repository
cases.note: The isolated workspace deliberately sits outside any git repository, which makes the refusal deterministic and keeps the case from creating a worktree in the developer's checkout. It smoked the success path by accident while the workspace lived under build/, leaving a real worktree and branch behind.

Smoked despite --verbose covering the same field, because the short letters diverge from 197 in a way a process can see: -v has to run a turn here, where 197 would print a version and exit. Reaching the marker is what distinguishes the two, so no extra expectation is needed.
No prompt and no server: the usage text is produced before anything that could reach the network.

The other half of the -v/-V divergence: version lives on -V here and on -v in 197. Smoking both letters is what keeps an attempt to align them from silently swapping which one prints a version and which one runs a turn.

notSmoked.print: print-p exercises the identical field and code path; the matrix already proves both spellings land in the same one.
notSmoked.input-format: stdin is the stream-json control protocol. Feeding it the empty stdin every other case uses would test the protocol reader, not startup.
notSmoked.combo-print-stream-json-stream-json: Same reason as input-format, which it contains.
notSmoked.add-dir: The single-value form is a parse-level distinction; the variadic case covers the process path.
notSmoked.add-dir-2: Comma-splitting is a parse-level distinction only.
notSmoked.add-dir-swallows-trailing-prompt: The whole assertion is a parse-level residual — that the trailing token becomes the prompt rather than a directory. A process cannot observe the difference.
notSmoked.worktree-2: Creating a named worktree mutates a git repository, and the isolated workspace deliberately sits outside one.
notSmoked.worktree-w: Same as worktree-2; the bare form already smokes the refusal path.
notSmoked.debug-2: The whole assertion is a parse-level residual — that 197's category filter becomes the initial prompt here rather than a debug filter. Both spellings end as a prompt sent to the model, so a process cannot observe which field the token landed in.
notSmoked.official-debug-file: The SDK transport test verifies argv mapping; a startup smoke would create a diagnostic artifact outside the transcript assertions.
notSmoked.official-include-hook-events: Hook-event emission requires a stream-json callback fixture and is covered with the SDK bidirectional protocol rather than one-shot startup.
notSmoked.official-session-mirror: Transcript mirror frames require a live stream-json consumer and SessionStore assertion, which belongs to the SDK transport tests.
notSmoked.official-allow-dangerously-skip-permissi: The meaningful behavior is a later SDK permission-mode transition; one-shot startup cannot distinguish allow from immediate bypass safely.
notSmoked.official-thinking-display: Thinking display affects partial stream rendering and needs a thinking-event fixture rather than the fixed one-shot smoke response.
notSmoked.official-task-budget: Task budget is consumed during nested task execution; the smoke server does not issue an Agent or other budgeted task.
notSmoked.official-fork-session: A valid process case needs a seeded resume target and a second transcript identity; this is covered by dedicated resume/fork tests.
notSmoked.official-no-session-persistence: The observable contract is the absence of a transcript, while this smoke harness expects a transcript for its normal marker assertions.
notSmoked.official-resume-session-at: A valid process case requires a seeded multi-message chain containing the selected UUID; dedicated resume fixtures cover that boundary.
notSmoked.official-rewind-files: A valid process case requires both a seeded transcript message UUID and a matching filesystem checkpoint; CliRewindFilesOperationTest covers the standalone restore and validation paths.
notSmoked.official-betas: The fixed fake response does not expose request beta headers; request-wire tests are the authoritative assertion for this option.
notSmoked.official-managed-settings: Managed policy precedence needs isolated policy sources and is covered by settings integration tests rather than the generic startup marker.
notSmoked.official-plugin-dir-no-mcp: Its distinction from plugin-dir is MCP suppression inside a populated plugin; an empty-directory startup smoke cannot observe it.
